result.process_description:
Consider a process for purchasing items from an online shop.
The user starts an order by logging in to their account.
Then, the user simultaneously selects the items to purchase and sets a payment method.
Afterward, the user either pays or completes an installment agreement.
After selecting the items, the user chooses between multiple options for a free reward.
Since the reward value depends on the purchase value, this step is done after selecting the items, but it is independent of the payment activities.
Finally, the items are delivered.
The user has the right to return items for exchange.
Every time items are returned, a new delivery is made.

result.rule: Use a parallel split when all outgoing branches start. Do not add decision conditions to parallel branches.
Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Use a parallel join when a shared continuation waits for all active parallel branches. Never use it to join mutually exclusive alternatives.
Use data input and output associations between data and activities. Data associations do not define execution order.
An ordinary embedded subprocess participates in normal sequence flow and may contain its own starts, ends, activities, gateways and flows.
Use bpmn:sequenceFlow for execution order between flow nodes in the same process or subprocess scope; set valid sourceRef and targetRef values.

result.rule: When the description lists two or more activities that are performed without a stated order and must all be completed before a later step begins: Model a parallel gateway that splits into one outgoing branch per listed activity, and a parallel gateway that joins those branches before the next step. Do not chain the activities in sequence, and do not use an exclusive gateway for them.

When the description lists two or more actions that must all be carried out after a common point, with no order or alternative stated between them, and only then leads to a later step: Model a parallel gateway that splits into one task per listed action, keeping each action as its own task with the description's wording, in a separate branch. Join all branches with a parallel gateway before the later step, so the later step waits for every action. Do not chain the actions in sequence, do not use an exclusive gateway for them, and do not leave any branch without a connecting flow to the join.

When the description lists several activities that are performed together with no stated order and must all be finished before a later step, and one of those activities happens only in certain cases, so it is conditional: Model each fixed activity as its own task in a separate branch of a parallel gateway split. Place the conditional activity behind an exclusive gateway inside its own branch, with one outgoing flow for the case where it happens and one for the case where it does not. Join all branches with a parallel gateway before the later step. Do not wrap these activities in an embedded subprocess, and do not chain them in sequence.

When the description says a later step starts once a condition or state is reached, and that state is reached when the concurrent activities running before it have progressed, without describing a wait for an external message, signal, time, or condition: Connect the parallel join that closes those concurrent activities directly to the task that starts the later step. Do not insert a separate intermediate catch event to represent the state being reached, because the join already represents that synchronization.
